auth.sign_in_to_continue: Sign in to continue working in FARI.
auth.workspace_description: Create Frames, manage assets and claims, preserve evidence and technical source files, normalize supplied material, and publish executive reports from one place.
auth.credentials: Default local credentials are fari / toor. Change them with FARI_LOGIN_USERNAME and FARI_LOGIN_PASSWORD.
auth.report_author_description: Authentication controls workspace access only. Generated reports still list Fari-Agent as the report author.
auth.access_description: Use the workspace credentials to continue into assessments, resources, and the internal FARI wiki.
page.assessment_workspace_title: Make every assessment easier to frame, review, and publish.
page.assessment_workspace_description: Review the most recent assessments first, filter by lifecycle and overall conclusion, and move from Frame to final consolidated reporting without losing traceability.
page.filtered_matches: Filtered matches sorted by latest activity
page.assessment_list_description: Newest activity first. Filter by lifecycle, executive outcome, and list size.
page.no_assessments: No assessments match the current filters
page.no_assessments_description: Reset the filters or create the first Frame. FARI will generate stable identifiers and guide the report to closure.
page.create_frame_description: Define the client, mission context, and boundaries that give every later conclusion meaning. A strong Frame reads like a defensible assessment brief, not just an internal note.
page.frame_step_1_hint: Start with the owner, the assessment name, and the mission reason.
page.frame_step_2_hint: Describe exactly what is included so future conclusions stay bounded.
page.frame_step_3_hint: Record authorization, safety limits, and explicit exclusions before work begins.
page.frame_save_hint: You can refine the Frame later from the assessment page.
page.frame_ready_note: Once this Frame is saved, FARI will guide you through assets, investigations, evidence, decisions, and versions.
page.client_name_help: Use the organization or mission-owner name that should appear in the report.
page.assessment_title_help: Keep it short but specific about the system and focus area.
page.mission_context_help: Mention mission role, operational environment, and why the outcome matters.
page.scope_help: List assets, environments, interfaces, data paths, and access limits. This is the guardrail for every conclusion.
page.authorization_help: Capture approvals, rules of engagement, stop conditions, and safety limits.
page.exclusions_help: State what the report must not be interpreted as proving.
page.investigation_intro: The claim identifier is generated automatically. Save normalization work freely; closure is a separate, explicit review action.
page.claim_step_1_hint: State the expected behavior, affected asset, method, environment, and boundary.
page.claim_step_2_hint: Separate facts, supplied assertions, inferences, assumptions, contradictions, and gaps.
page.claim_step_3_hint: Choose the conclusion, confidence, priority, action, and objective follow-up.
page.claim_wording_help: Meets means this exact expected behavior was supported. It is not a severity score.
page.claim_save_hint: You can return to this step while the investigation remains open.
page.result_save_hint: Saving this result does not close the investigation. Closure is an explicit review action on the detail page.
page.claim_description_help: The claim should be narrow enough that Meets, Does Not Meet, or Inconclusive answer something concrete.
page.close_scope_help: This prevents a lab-only or document-only result from being overstated as mission-wide proof.
page.gating_claim: This is a gating claim for the consolidated conclusion
page.normalize_material_description: Use one statement per line. Validation errors preserve every submitted field.
page.investigation_list_hint: Each claim has its own evidence, decision, and next action.
page.asset_register_hint: Name the systems that conclusions will refer to.
page.inventory_section_hint: Keep source files and technical inventory changes traceable per asset.
page.no_investigations: No investigations yet. Create one after registering the relevant assets.
page.no_assets: Add at least one asset so investigations can reference the affected system.
page.no_inventory: No inventory components yet. Add a source to an asset to start a traceable component timeline.
page.no_asset_sources: No source files have been preserved for this asset yet.
page.gating_not_severity: Derived from gating claims · not a severity score
page.register_asset_description: Describe the asset so later evidence, source files, claims, and conclusions can reference it precisely. Use Other when the segment or access basis does not fit a single predefined option.
page.asset_name_help: Name the system exactly as it should be referenced by investigations and evidence.
page.asset_description_help: Briefly explain what the asset does and where it sits. This helps the report read clearly without reopening the raw evidence.
page.no_inventory_components: No inventory components yet. Add a source to an asset to start a traceable component timeline.
page.snapshot_placeholder: Why this revision matters: new evidence, normalized findings, pre-close review, source refresh...
page.choose_different_states: Choose two different states to compare.
page.no_differences: No differences were found between the selected states.
page.close_investigation_confirm: Close this investigation permanently? It cannot be reopened or edited afterward.
page.close_investigation_button: Close permanently and publish final report
page.no_findings_detail: No normalized findings yet. Findings are optional when the evidence does not support one.
page.inventory_detail_description: Review the asset component timeline, linked source files, and traceable status changes.
page.traceability_description: Compare captured revisions against the current working state or against prior snapshots. This is the executive audit trail for how the assessment moved from draft to conclusion.
page.upload_inventory_description: Sources can be dependency inventories, JSON Lines / NDJSON logs, SigMF metadata or data, packet captures, text files, documents, binary samples, and other technical formats.
page.source_register_hint: Keep raw files, hashes, formats, and derived inventory together with the asset.
page.asset_source_description: Upload the raw material associated with this asset. FARI preserves the original bytes and SHA-256 while extracting structured inventory only when the format supports it.
page.source_formats: Accepted: binaries, SigMF, PCAP/PCAPNG, JSON/JSONL, CSV/TSV, YAML/XML, text, documents, archives, and unknown extensions.
page.no_asset_components: No normalized components are linked to this asset yet.
page.no_asset_investigations: No investigations are linked to this asset yet.
page.publish_decision_description: The overall claim conclusion is derived from gating claims. Scenario dispositions remain visible separately so a plausible attack path is not hidden by claim wording or converted into a severity score.
page.before_closing: Before closing: confirm every gating investigation is immutable and its required action is understood.
page.close_report_button: Close permanently and publish final report
page.close_confirm: Close this assessment permanently? It cannot be reopened or changed afterward.
page.edit_finding_description: Update the normalized finding and its optional framework mapping before the investigation is closed.
page.no_findings: No normalized findings yet. Findings are optional when the evidence does not support one.
page.resources_description: This page keeps the manual FARI artifacts close to the guided workflow so the web app, markdown templates, and canonical specification stay aligned.
page.wiki_description: This wiki is rendered from the canonical specification document used to align the framework, the manual template, and the web workflow.
